facts.text: The BTS Skytrain and MRT subway are clean, air-conditioned, and skip Bangkok's notorious traffic entirely; tuk-tuks look charming but routinely quote tourists several times a metered taxi's fare for the same trip.

Street food runs roughly ฿40-80 a dish (~$1-2), a full restaurant meal for two is closer to $15-25, and a mid-range hotel is roughly ฿1,200-2,800/night (~$35-90) - genuinely one of the cheaper major destinations for eating well.

Tuk-tuk drivers near the Grand Palace offering a suspiciously cheap ride often steer riders toward a commission-paying gem or tailor shop instead of the intended destination - agree a price or use the meter before getting in, and treat "that temple is closed today" as a scam line.
The Grand Palace enforces a strict dress code (no shorts, no sleeveless tops) and turns away visitors at the gate for it - bring a cover-up rather than relying on rentals at the entrance.
Heat and humidity are intense nearly year-round; plan major walking or outdoor sightseeing for early morning rather than midday.

Vegetarian and vegan street food is genuinely abundant if you know to ask for "mangsawirat" (vegetarian) - without asking, fish sauce and shrimp paste show up in dishes that otherwise look plant-based.
